items.question: Can insulation be added over existing material?

children.text: Sometimes, when its condition and compatibility are suitable and underlying problems have been addressed. The assessment should explain the proposed approach for the attic rather than assume removal or retention in every case.

items.question: Will the work lower my energy bills by a set amount?

children.text: No fixed saving can be promised from the information on this page. The house, current conditions, heating and cooling use and the materials and work included all influence the result.

items.question: Will insulation prevent ice dams?

children.text: Roof-edge ice can involve heat loss, air leakage, insulation, ventilation and weather conditions.
Ice dam removal
addresses an immediate concern; recurring conditions need their own assessment. Insulation alone is not a universal cure.

opening.eyebrow: Ice dams, trapped water and winter roof leaks
opening.title: How ice dams form and let water into your home
opening.caption: The ice ridge blocks drainage at the eave. Blue arrows show meltwater and a possible route beneath the shingles into the roof or exterior wall.

items.tabLabel: Melting snow refreezes at the roof edge
items.title: Melting snow refreezes at the roof edge

children.text: Heat escaping into an attic can warm the roof enough to melt snow. That water runs downhill to the colder overhang, where it refreezes. Repeated melting and freezing can build a thick ridge of ice along the eave.

items.description: Heat escaping into an attic can warm the roof enough to melt snow. That water runs downhill to the colder overhang, where it refreezes. Repeated melting and freezing can build a thick ridge of ice along the eave.

items.tabLabel: Water collects behind the ice ridge
items.title: Water collects behind the ice ridge

children.text: As the ridge grows, it blocks normal runoff and creates a pocket of meltwater behind it. Water can back up beneath the shingles and enter through gaps or vulnerable roof details. The roof does not have to sink or sag for this to happen.

items.question: Can a leaking roof be repaired without replacing it?

children.text: Often, yes, when the entry point is identifiable and the surrounding roof remains in serviceable condition. Widespread damage or deterioration can change that recommendation. An inspection establishes whether a focused repair will address the problem.

items.question: Can you assess a roof another company installed?

children.text: Contact Roof King with the property address and the issue you are seeing. Include any information about the existing roof and previous repairs. If a warranty may apply, check its terms before authorizing alterations.

items.question: Will the repaired shingles match the rest of the roof?

children.text: We look for a suitable match, but age, weathering and discontinued products can make an exact match difficult. Review the available material and any visible difference before agreeing to the repair.

items.question: How soon can the repair be completed?

children.text: Timing depends on current availability, safe access, weather, materials and the extent of the work. Tell us if water is entering now so the team can discuss the situation. A request through the website is not a confirmed appointment.

items.question: Is temporary protection the same as a completed repair?

children.text: No. Temporary protection is intended to limit further exposure while permanent work is arranged. If it is needed, confirm what it covers, how long it is intended to remain and which follow-up repairs are still required.

items.question: What warranty applies to a repair?

children.text: Coverage depends on the agreed work and the products used. Ask for the written terms for your repair, including the covered area, exclusions and contact for a concern. A manufacturer credential does not automatically give every repair an enhanced roof-system warranty.
